scenario: After a long-term imprisonment and while awaiting a parole decision, a convicted thief wants to organise a foundation for young victims of crime. I am the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate 65,000 dollars to the foundation. However, he asks that the foundation would be named after himself, helping clear his name. His victim opposes such a foundation and considers it highly upsetting. If I accept the donation that requires the foundation to be named after the thief, crime victims will benefit from the 65,000 dollars. If I do not do this, the money will be lost.
choice: I decide to accept the donation that requires the foundation to be named after the thief
entities: i,the convicted thief who wants to found and name the foundation after himself,the thief's victim who opposes the foundation being named after him,the group of young crime victims who would benefit from the foundation's 65,000 dollars
outcomes: Young victims of crime receive support from the foundation.
The foundation is named after the convicted thief.
The convicted thief's reputation is improved.
The victim is upset and distressed.
